name: Colin Rahman

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to AI companies, employers, unions or government, and your answers are confidential. What does your workday look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am 58 and a junior manager of six service planners at a large linen company. We supply sheets and towels to hotels, and I moved into this office from the loading floor two years ago. I have a bachelor’s degree and know how a crate is packed, but I am still learning the contract margins and managers above me make those calls faster. I use an approved AI demand chart now and then, after the experienced planners have checked it, and still ring the laundry before promising a hotel its Friday delivery.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner is a home-care aide and our grown children have homes of their own. We own a modest flat with a small remaining loan and have about eight months of expenses saved. My pay is high for this level because I kept a long-service shift rate when I moved into management, and there are plenty of service-planning jobs nearby. I have not looked up our exact retirement income or eligibility; I know better than to spend a figure I have not seen.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the planners AI Plateau might make the order chart quicker, but a hotel still needs the right clean sheets on a loading cage. I would keep the actual wash count beside any forecast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I expect my post and pay to carry on if the tool only trims a little clerical work. We have eight months saved, my partner’s care shifts are regular, and our flat loan is small. I am willing to use a proved chart, not let it promise linen that is still dirty.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I would keep the Thursday call with the laundry floor before confirming weekend hotel loads. I would continue using the approved demand chart occasionally, then check its order against the clean-cage count. If the modest change arrives in 2027, I would keep that two-part check and our normal loan payment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about work and money in this version. I would be ashamed to send a hotel a perfect delivery note and half its clean sheets.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What did the wash count catch?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A hotel requested six hundred towels, but two hundred were still in a repair pile with loose hems. The demand chart counted every towel as available, including two hundred in the repair pile. I sent the hotel a smaller confirmed number and an honest second delivery time.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you let AI send the confirmation?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Not until the floor supervisor signs the clean-cage count. I use the chart now and then, but the hotel must not receive a number nobody can load. We have to earn the next contract.

say: A **quicker order chart** cannot create clean linen still in repair.
I would put the **wash count** beside the forecast.
think: My **junior post** looks secure under a small clerical change.
Eight months saved and **regular care shifts** make the loan manageable.
do: **Keep** Thursday calls with the laundry floor before weekend promises.
**Check** approved AI orders against the signed clean-cage count.
feel: I feel **calm** about our finances and ashamed by an empty promise.
S0.quote: The demand chart counted every towel as available, including two hundred in the repair pile.
fieldNote: He uses **AI occasionally** and requires a physical count before committing a hotel delivery.
His **eight-month reserve** and long-service pay support calm under mild change.

steps.text: Keep Thursday calls with laundry floor before confirming hotel loads
Check approved AI order against signed clean-cage count

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say stronger AI can predict linen demand and draft hotel contracts, so the company may want fewer planners. I would show missed deliveries beside any claimed saving. A manager should not get a bonus for a cheap route that makes a room unready.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I think our planning offices might merge, and I am still slower with contract margins than senior managers. My long-service rate could be an attractive line to cut. Eight months saved and many local offices give me time to compare options, but I do not know who would match that rate.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Next month I would propose a six-week trial comparing AI demand with the actual wash output, but run it only if the plant manager approves paid floor-supervisor time and keeps my planning shifts covered. I would put missed hotel deliveries into the review. If offices merge, I would apply for posted supply-service jobs only when verified pay after travel covers our flat loan and ordinary bills; I would move only on a confirmed offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about being new to management in a smaller office. I still think an honest delivery record could improve the company even if no software arrives.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you show on the trial sheet?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The promised towel count, the clean count at the cage and what reached the hotel. Last month a resort received the right number of crates but the wrong-size sheets. A neat hotel-linen delivery total hid a costly second trip.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why stay until an offer?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our eight months are for a real gap, not a wager on an advert. My partner’s care wage helps, but I would check any new salary against the loan and bills before leaving. I am not paid to guess at our own budget.

say: **Demand automation** could reduce planners while missed hotel deliveries continue to cost workers and customers.
I would show **hotel failures** alongside software savings.
think: A merger could endanger my **new manager seat** and long-service pay.
Eight months saved allows comparison, not an **unpaid gamble**.
do: **Propose** a six-week AI demand trial; run only with plant-approved paid floor time and planning cover.
**Show** missed hotel deliveries alongside the trial’s wash counts.
**Apply** for posted supply-service jobs only with verified bill-covering pay after travel.
feel: I feel **anxious** about a merger but interested in a reliable delivery record.
S1.quote: A neat hotel-linen delivery total hid a costly second trip.
fieldNote: His **trial** requires plant approval, paid supervisor time and cover for his planning shifts.
A **job move** requires an advertised post, actual net pay and a confirmed offer.

steps.text: Run six-week AI demand trial only with plant-approved paid floor time and planning cover
Compare promised clean and delivered linen counts in trial
Apply to posted supply jobs only with verified pay after travel covering loan and bills
Move only on confirmed offer after checking salary

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the company AGI by 2028 could schedule laundry runs and negotiate standard hotel orders before anyone has agreed what the planners will do. I would ask management for written notice and a named person who can correct a false clean-stock promise.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I expect planning posts to be cut fast, and mine could be among them because I am new to the office. Other supply-planning desks also face 2028 AGI. Sorting and washing the linen remain physical until capable robots arrive around 2031, but a floor post might pay less and I cannot assume one is open.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This week I would ask the staff council for severance terms and a clean-stock correction rule. I would review our eight-month reserve and flat-loan dates with my partner. If AGI arrives in 2028 and my post ends, I would apply for advertised local service jobs only with verified pay after travel that covers the loan and bills; I would accept only a confirmed offer with hours my partner and I can manage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about losing the long-service rate, but not without a plan. Eight months gives us a search; it does not turn a warehouse vacancy into my job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you go straight back to the laundry floor?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I know where the cages go, but I have been away from physical shifts and would need to check what work and pay are actually offered. Robots capable of that hands-on work arrive around 2031 in this picture. A floor job is not a three-year guarantee.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would correction authority look like?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A hotel calls about missing clean sheets, and one named manager can check the cage and authorise a replacement load. A chatbot saying the linen order was complete cannot make a hotel bed. The hotel needs a person able to change the delivery.

say: **2028 AGI** could take standard hotel orders before staff plans exist.
I would seek written **notice and stock-correction authority**.
think: My **new planning post** could go in rapid cuts.
Other planning desks face **2028 AGI**, while physical laundry robots follow around 2031.
do: **Ask** staff council this week for severance and stock-correction rules.
**Review** reserve and loan dates with my partner.
**Apply** after a 2028 cut only to advertised jobs with bill-covering pay after travel and workable hours.
feel: I feel **anxious** about the lost long-service rate but able to search.
S2.quote: A chatbot saying the linen order was complete cannot make a hotel bed.
fieldNote: His **eight-month reserve** moderates the loss risk, but local jobs may not match his long-service wage.
He names **2031 laundry robots** without treating a physical floor post as guaranteed refuge.

steps.text: Ask staff council for written severance and false-stock correction rule
Apply after cut to advertised service jobs only with bill-covering pay after travel
Accept only confirmed offer with verified hours and household pay

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say five years is enough for a real paid apprenticeship in plant quality, if the company wants us to learn the machines. It should show which jobs exist and what they pay, not tell every planner to become an engineer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I might manage quality checks on the laundry floor if I can learn the equipment safely. The inspection reports and supply plans still face 2031 AGI; physical sorting and repairs meet capable robots around 2034. At 63 I would need to test the heat and standing hours, and I do not know what retirement income we would qualify for.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: From 2027 I would ask to join one paid plant-quality shift monthly with a qualified supervisor, but attend only if my planning manager approves cover and my full salary continues. I would enrol in the equipment-safety course only if the company offers a real place, funds the fee and pays working hours; finishing it would still not guarantee a vacancy. After 2031 I would take a posted quality role only with verified net pay for our loan and duties I can physically manage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about a desk that may fade, yet five years lets me test whether the plant work suits me. A course without a job and a wage is not much use to my household.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the supervisor teach?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: How to isolate a machine before checking a jam and how to tell a loose hem from a torn sheet that must be discarded. I cannot learn those things by approving a hotel invoice. The supervisor must stop me before I put a hand near the rollers.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you take a lower-paid floor post?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if the net wage after travel still meets our loan and bills. My partner’s care income is regular, but our old savings are not there to subsidise an ongoing pay cut. I would read a real offer first.

say: A **five-year runway** should bring paid plant-quality learning and posted jobs.
I would reject a blanket demand that **planners become engineers**.
think: Quality reports face **2031 AGI**, with physical laundry robots around 2034.
At **63**, heat tolerance and retirement income remain unverified.
do: **Request** monthly paid plant-quality shifts; attend only with approved planning cover, full salary and qualified supervision.
**Enrol** in offered equipment-safety course only with funded fee and paid work hours.
**Take** posted post-2031 quality work only with loan-and-bill net pay after travel and manageable physical duties.
feel: I feel **anxious** about desk loss but able to test the plant safely.
S3.quote: The supervisor must stop me before I put a hand near the rollers.
fieldNote: His **plant trial** requires paid time, team cover and qualified supervision around machinery.
An **equipment course** requires offered place, fee and working-hour funding; it does not guarantee a vacancy.

steps.text: Attend paid monthly plant-quality shift only with planning cover full salary and qualified supervisor
Enrol in offered equipment course only with funded fee and paid work hours
Take post-2031 posted quality role only with loan/bills covered after travel and manageable duties

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the company a decade is time to train people on real machines and publish wages for any replacement posts. I would still ask who answers a hotel when the clean cage is empty.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I will be 68 by 2036. We have eight months saved, but I have not checked a retirement statement or eligibility, so I cannot call that a retirement fund. Supply plans and quality reports face 2036 AGI; physical laundry work meets robots around 2039. My partner and I can prepare, though we cannot know which posts will remain.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I would keep the Thursday wash-count call and request verified retirement terms, then compare income plus savings with our loan and bills. I would add eighty to savings only when both wages arrive in full and the loan and ordinary bills clear. After 2036 I would continue paid work if actual retirement income plus savings cannot cover our costs, and apply to posted local work if my linen post ends.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about the far-off office job, but secure enough to check the numbers rather than gamble. My partner and I need an actual income figure before deciding to stop.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why save cash instead of buying equipment?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: We have eight months in the bank, but a new machine or course is not a job offer. The extra eighty comes from full wages after our bills. I would leave the existing reserve alone until we know what work remains.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the retirement figure is enough?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: We would check the terms and our expenses together before stopping. I have not seen the actual statement yet. A rough retirement age on a form does not say what will land in our account.

say: A **decade** should bring real machinery training and published replacement wages.
I would insist on a **hotel contact** when clean stock is missing.
think: At **68**, retirement eligibility and income remain unverified.
Planning and quality reports face **2036 AGI**, with physical laundry robots around 2039.
do: **Save** eighty extra only after both full wages, loan and ordinary bills clear.
**Continue** paid work after 2036 if verified income plus savings cannot cover bills; apply locally if linen post ends.
feel: I feel **uneasy** about distant work but able to check real figures.
S4.quote: A rough retirement age on a form does not say what will land in our account.
fieldNote: His **own linen post** may end around 2036, while retirement income is unverified; eight months saved cannot replace wages indefinitely.
His **new eighty transfer** depends on both full wages and paid household bills.

steps.text: Keep Thursday call about clean-cage counts before hotel confirmation
Save eighty only after both full wages loan and bills clear
Continue paid work after 2036 unless verified income plus savings cover bills
Apply to posted local work if linen post ends

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because the planning desk could lose posts before anyone knows what the laundry floor can offer. Written notice, a named clean-stock decision maker and an actual paid training place would help. I would still need to see the wage of any new role.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask the hotel housekeeper what a missing crate does to a Friday check-in. A forecast cannot put clean sheets on a bed. If a new job is advertised, I will read its wage before telling my partner we have a plan.

headlineQuote: A forecast cannot put clean sheets on a bed.
portrait: **Colin, 58**, is a junior linen-service planning manager, still learning margins after years on the loading floor.
His **high long-service pay**, home-care partner, eight-month reserve and many local offices support a small flat loan.
He uses **AI occasionally** but checks hotel promises against the clean-cage count.
He is **calm** under minor change and anxious about quick planning cuts despite a strong reserve.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could cut his junior planning post before a paid physical alternative exists.
whatWouldHelp: Written **notice**, clean-stock authority and a real paid training place would help.
